Hi Karthik,

Specifically: can we avoid a big front-loaded hit to our ledger in Q1 and instead have a laddered drawdown (monthly/quarterly) tied to usage, while still qualifying for a term discount?

Key asks from our side:
- Spread the prepay consumption over each quarter (or monthly) rather than a single wallet depletion
- A predictable discount schedule for a 2-year vs 3-year committed spend
- True-up process at year-end (or quarterly) if we under/over-use

Have you seen this structure with other customers? If yes, what are typical discount bands and minimum guarantees (if any)?

Would like to get this in writing so procurement can build it into the SOW.

Hi Alice — great question and definitely solvable. We’ve done two common patterns that balance your goals:

1) Laddered wallet with quarterly anchors + annual true-up (recommended)
   - Commit amount placed in a "contract wallet" but drawdown is scheduled across 4 quarters with a small monthly smoothing factor.
   - Quarterly anchors (e.g., 25% each quarter) ensure predictability for both sides. If usage exceeds an anchor, remaining wallet is pulled; if underuse, a true-up at year-end adjusts the overage/credit.

2) Usage-first prepay with minimum annual guarantee
   - Lower upfront discount but a guaranteed minimum spend that triggers partial rebate or carry-forward. Useful if you want less up-front cash outlay.

Typical commercial bands we see: 6–12% off list for 2-year committed spends depending on mixed model/embedding volume and payment cadence; 10–16% for 3-year with staged ramps. We can tailor banding to your ramp profile in CS_Ramp_Schedule_v2.xlsx (attached).

Operational notes: monthly reconciliation and token-level reporting are standard; we can add a monthly cadence for internal ops & finance syncs. Legal usually asks for a simple failure-to-meet clause (e.g., discount steps down by X% if less than Y% of committed spend is consumed in a rolling 12-month window).

I’m attaching a ramp schedule template and a draft SOW excerpt to show where the true-up and anchor language lives. Suggest a 30-minute call with your procurement + finance to align on tolerance bands.

Next steps:
- Review the attached ramp schedule
- Confirm whether you prefer quarterly anchors or monthly smoothing
- If quarterly, we’ll surface the discount bands and produce a redlineable SOW

Hi Alice — based on internal alignment, here are two packaged options for CloudScale to consider (attached: redwood-draft-sow-v3.pdf):

Option A — Quarterly-anchored wallet (Recommended)
- 2-year: 8% term discount (if >=60% annual consumption)
- 3-year: 12% term discount (if >=65% annual consumption)
- Quarterly anchors: ~25% of contract wallet targeted to each quarter (monthly smoothing within quarter)
- Annual true-up with carry-forward up to 1 quarter for over-usage; under-usage remediation ladder as per legal note

Option B — Monthly-smoothed consumption
- 2-year: 5% term discount
- 3-year: 9% term discount
- No minimum guarantee; monthly reconciliation and reporting; smaller up-front discount reflects lower cash commitment

We can also insert a rollover clause that allows one-time carry-forward of up to 15% of unused wallet to the following contract year for 3-year deals (subject to reconciliation).

If either option looks good I’ll ask legal to publish a redline and we’ll route for signature (DocuSign link to follow). If you want to preserve more flexibility, Option B is the lower-risk route.

Thoughts? Happy to take a 30-min call with your finance & procurement to go over the operating mechanics.

Best,
Karthik
